_comment: Which AIs can do the work, what each costs, and which one a kind of task goes to. @workshop reads this to route a story (#alias on the story) and agents.py reads it to start the agent. ONE COPY: prices live here and nowhere else. A project may override it with docs/models.json. Prices are USD per million tokens, input / output (cache: read / write, when it differs from Anthropic's 0.1x / 2x of input -- Claude Code writes the 1-hour cache), checked 2026-10-27 (Anthropic: the API price list; DeepSeek: api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing, off-peak, peak is double). Update them when they change, and say so in the commit.

anthropic.name: Claude (Anthropic)
anthropic.how: Claude Code as you are logged in. Nothing else to set.

deepseek.name: DeepSeek
deepseek.how: Runs INSIDE Claude Code (same tools, skills, CLAUDE.md), pointed at DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible endpoint. Needs your DeepSeek API key in the environment variable named by key_env.

fable.good_for: the hardest reasoning: a whole phase's plan, a design nobody can agree on. Rarely worth it for one ticket.

opus.good_for: deciding: design, debugging an unknown cause, review, routing. The default for judgement.

opus-low.good_for: a strong model on a short leash: reading and summarising, small judged edits. Often cheaper per finished task than a weaker model that needs two tries.

sonnet.good_for: everyday building: a well-specified change with its tests, following a pattern the repo already has.

haiku.good_for: mechanical work with a fixed recipe: rename, reformat, run a script and report what it printed.

ds-pro.good_for: long, patient digging when the answer can be checked: reverse engineering, porting with a test to compare against. No images.

ds-flash.good_for: routine building and searching at a fraction of the price, where a test or a diff will catch a mistake.

ds-flash-low.good_for: the cheapest seat there is: mechanical edits, collecting facts, reformatting, first drafts someone else checks.

routing._comment: Kinds of task, cheapest acceptable first. @workshop names the kind; the first alias whose provider you have is used. A story's own #alias always wins. These are STARTING GUESSES: the retrospective moves a kind up or down from agents.py report, never from theory.

mechanical.what: a fixed recipe, nothing to decide: rename, reformat, move, run a script and report, fill a table from known facts

routine.what: a well-specified change with a check that catches mistakes; the repo already has the pattern

digging.what: long patient work whose result can be checked: reverse engineering, porting against a reference, searching many files

hard.what: deciding: a design choice, a bug whose cause is unknown, anything where a wrong answer looks right

judgement.what: review, retrospective, routing and planning: judging someone else's work or deciding who does what

sizes._comment: What one story of each size (~XS .. ~XL in its text) uses, in tokens over its whole session. Most of an agent's tokens are cache READS: every step re-reads the conversation. STARTING GUESSES, scaled from one measured 1-step task (31k read, 12k write, 330 out): agents.py report prints the measured median per size next to these, and the retrospective replaces them. An unsized story counts as M and is flagged.

XS.what: one step: a rename, a lookup

M.what: a feature's worth of edits with its tests

L.what: many files, several rounds of test and fix

XL.what: a session's limit: split it if you can

escalate: A story that fails its evidence on a model goes one kind up (mechanical -> routine -> hard) for the next try, not the same model again. agents.py report shows where that happens; the retrospective moves the routing table.

agents._comment: How agents.py runs a seat unattended. A headless agent cannot ask for permission, so what it may do is decided here. acceptEdits lets it edit files in the project; allowed_tools adds what it may run without asking. Tighten this for a project you do not trust an agent with.
